Sky News politics live blog — updated Thursday 24 September 2026 18:06 BST (posts timed 07:29, 08:08, 08:37, 08:58, 09:43, 10:20, 13:06 BST)

HEADLINE: 781 small boat migrants crossed the Channel on Wednesday 23 Sept — highest single day of 2026.

FACTS (Sky News live blog, 07:29 BST):
- 781 people crossed in 10 small boats on Wednesday; beats previous 2026 record of 752 people in 9 boats on 29 July.
- 18,565 migrants have crossed so far in 2026, including 6,096 since Andy Burnham became PM in July.
- 2026 total is down around 42-45% on the same point last year; 49% fewer boats.
- Wednesday's figure is only the 31st highest 24-hour total since records began in 2018; the highest was September 2022, when more than 1,300 crossed in a day.
- On 10 August 2026 a record 230 people arrived on a single dinghy.
- Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood ordered an "urgent review" after Border Force failed to intercept two boats on successive days — one landed at Folkestone on Monday morning (first undetected arrival in over a year), a second at Dover on Tuesday afternoon.
- 83,279 people have crossed the Channel since Labour came to power 812 days ago (Home Office data cited by Sky). Sky Data & Forensics notes 83,500 crossed in the equivalent final 812 days of the Conservative government — 221 more.

QUOTES:
Government spokesperson (Home Office), Sky News 08:08 BST:
"Our progress this year in tackling small boats is indisputable – with crossings down by 42% and the lowest recorded over the summer months since 2020. But this week's events show that while the peaks we are seeing are far below those of previous years, we need to push further and harder in order to eradicate this vile trade."

Nigel Farage, Reform UK leader, Sky News 08:37 BST:
"781 illegal migrants invaded Britain yesterday. But don't worry, Andy Burnham is making a TikTok. Reform will deploy the Royal Navy and stop the boats."
Farage also said the Channel situation is "insane" and added: "Labour have totally lost control of our borders."
Richard Tice, Reform deputy leader, same post: "illegals are laughing at Open Borders Burnham" — said Reform's plan will "save lives and save British taxpayers billions, as well as protecting our women and girls from these criminals".

Chris Philp, shadow home secretary, Sky News 09:43 BST:
"Labour has let an entire army-sized population cross the Channel illegally. More people have arrived in small boats than we have soldiers defending Britain. That is completely bonkers."
"Labour has lost control of our borders and seems utterly incapable of getting it back. The Conservative plan is to end hotels and benefits for illegal immigrants and instead deport them."

ALSO ON THE BLOG:
- Anti-migrant protester Daniel Thomas ("Danny Tommo"), 37, of no fixed abode, arrested Wednesday night on suspicion of criminal damage with intent to endanger life, destroying ships/endangering safety (s.11 Aviation and Maritime Security Act 1990) and conduct endangering ships (s.58 Merchant Shipping Act 1995) — Hampshire Police statement. He had posted video appearing to show himself slashing an inflatable with a knife while shouting "traitors", with a rescue crew member aboard.
- Justice Secretary Alex Norris (10:20 BST) on court backlog record high and jury trials: "In 2010 there were 29,000 magistrates. The Tory government let that fall to as low as 12,000 - we've got that up to 15,500. But through our campaign we want to get to 21,000 magistrates." On scrapping jury trials: "people have raised really important concerns about this. So the prime minister is a new prime minister, [I am] a new minister responsible for the justice system. We are looking at that again. And when we bring back the bill in October, that will reflect those things that we've heard."
- Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband (13:06 BST) announced a Gaza aid package, part of an £88m bundle: "It is vital that civilians in Gaza have unhindered access to aid. The UK is pledging a major new package of aid to provide much needed healthcare support to those desperately in need. We urge the government of Israel to listen to our call to action and take steps to end its unacceptable restrictions on Gaza." Package: medical consultations for up to 900,000 people; rehabilitation and prosthetics for 1,000 children with blast injuries; solid waste management for up to 900,000; emergency water trucking for 150,000; mental health support for 21,000. Part of £127m allocated to Palestine in UK ODA budget for 2026/27.
- Green Party conference row over a motion characterising Zionism as "racism"; leader Zack Polanski has called for changes to it. Conference in just over a week.
